correctness.rationale: The one-vertex Bernoulli-product representation is exact. For each tail class, first-k-consecutive-child events give the lower marginal exponent, a generating-product Markov bound gives the upper exponent, and disjoint length-k arrival blocks give independent witnesses despite inter-vertex dependence. Union bounds and dyadic Borel–Cantelli with monotone interpolation prove the stated two almost-sure maxima. Exact finite-state geometric diagnostics passed 398 rational assertions but are explicitly not substitutes for the infinite proof.

Classical extreme-value overlap and inaccessible renewal-forest full text remain stated priority risks, so originality is best-knowledge and not independently confirmed.

value.rationale: The literature establishes a natural random-forest maximum-degree question with a distribution-free upper bound. The new sharp scale distinguishes geometric/stretched-exponential laws from summable polynomial lags and gives a nontrivial tail-dependent coefficient in the latter. It supplies a structural dependent-extreme-value argument and quantifies the effect of a natural modeling parameter, rather than merely refining constants in a routine finite calculation.
